results.resolution: Second independent grading found. The 1981 regional alpine guide (North Cascades volume) describes the climb of East Twin Needle from the dividing notch (the Eye Col) as one difficult ~50 ft pitch and then a class 4 pitch to the summit ridge, graded 'Class 5.6 and aid'. The 2009 party graded the same section's crux 5.7 free. The two accounts are 41 years apart and agree that this line is low fifth class, nowhere near 5.10a. The live grade (II, 5.7, applied in s4 on one source) therefore stands. 5.7 is kept because it is the only free-climbing grade either source gives; the 1968 grade includes a point of aid. Two text ops bring data_quality.gaps[0] and corrections up to date, since they still say the grade rests on one account. Grade fields are not changed.
results.summary: A second, much older account of the climb from the Eye Col also grades it low fifth class (5.6 with a point of aid), so the page's 5.7 grade is now backed by two independent ascents and its notes say so.
results.evidence: NEW SOURCE: the regional alpine guide, 1981 edition (Rainy Pass to Fraser River), was read through the Internet Archive full-text search. The volume is lending-restricted; only search snippets were read, chained phrase by phrase, with no borrowing and no bypass. Its EAST TWIN NEEDLE entry reads: first ascent by the West Twin Needle 1968 party, which 'continued the route from the dividing notch with a difficult pitch, some 50 ft in height to a good belay stance'. That pitch went right, then left, on piton protection and one aid chock. 'The next pitch (class 4) ends on the knifed summit ridge. Class 5.6 and aid.' The entry cites the 1969 American Alpine Journal. That journal's note, found by the same search, reports the 1968 party's ascent of East Twin Needle and says an earlier credited first ascent of the East Needle was in error. It is the same ascent as the guide, so it counts as one source with it. ALREADY KNOWN (not re-counted): the 2009 Thread of Ice party climbed East Twin from the Eye Col with a crux '5.7 handcrack' (the photographer's trip report and the regional journal's short note on it). Independence: one is the 1968 first-ascent party via the guide and journal, the other the 2009 party; they share no author or citation. PROPOSED WORDING (no source names): gaps[0] and corrections are rewritten to say two ascents grade the line 5.6 with a point of aid and 5.7 free. FLAG FOR THE OWNER (no op): the overview says both needles were first climbed together on August 17, 1932 by Degenhardt, Martin and Strandberg. The 1981 guide gives East Twin's first ascent to the 1968 party, and the 1969 journal note calls the earlier East Needle credit erroneous. Those two are one lineage, though, and the guide's other book says only that the 1932 party climbed 'one of the twin needles'. So the sentence is probably wrong for East Twin, but it is left as it is pending a second independent source.
sources: Cascade Alpine Guide: Rainy Pass to Fraser River (1981), East Twin Needle entry, via Internet Archive full-text search
American Alpine Journal 1969, Southern Pickets / East Twin Needle note, via Internet Archive full-text search (same lineage as the guide)
Steph Abegg 2009 Twin Needles trip report (already known)
